Goals: - A running chain's reports appear in an open page without anyone restarting or reloading anything.
- The refresh mechanism costs almost nothing when nothing is happening and adds no dependency to detect change.
- Every screen of the client and every job of the server has its own file, with a size limit that is checked rather than hoped for.
- A host module has a test module, and a failing check names the unit that broke.
Key product decisions: - Use structured input as the source of truth for generated docs.
- Keep generated write paths local and repo-bounded.
Overview: Turns the served viewer into a live view onto the reports directory instead of a snapshot, and gives both sides of it -- the host code and the page -- a module structure, a size budget and a real test layout, so the next slice edits a small file instead of the only file.

Acceptance criteria: - AC1: The served page's payload is fetched from the server rather than read from a build-time file, and a page opened from disk keeps working exactly as it does today from its generated fallback.
- AC2: A served page reflects a new, changed or removed report without the operator restarting the server or reloading the page, within a few seconds of the file landing.

- AC3: Change detection uses the standard library only -- no file-watching dependency -- and its cost is bounded so that an idle viewer does not consume a meaningful share of a core; the bound is stated and measured, not asserted.
- AC4: The event stream carries what changed, not the changed data, and the client refetches only the affected part; no code path in the client reloads the whole page on a data change.
- AC5: A client with no event-stream support still converges on fresh data through a self-throttling fallback, and neither path leaves a timer or a connection running after the page is closed.

- AC6: `adr_004` is amended (or superseded) to record that the auto-refresh it promised now exists and how, and to record the build step the client split requires -- with the rejected alternative named.
Needs: - `adr_004` states that `meshanvil view --serve` starts a server `for auto-refresh`. Nothing auto-refreshes: there is no watcher, no event stream and no polling anywhere in `meshanvil/viewer.py` or `viewer/viewer.js`. The promise is documented and was never built, so an operator watching a chain run has to stop the server, re-run the command and reopen the page to see the report that just landed.

- Even a manual browser refresh shows nothing new: the payload is baked into `work/viewer/data.js` at build time, so the page is a snapshot of the moment the command ran rather than a view onto the reports directory.

- `viewer/viewer.js` is 908 lines in one file covering every screen, every renderer and every event handler. Each slice that touches the viewer -- and the last four have -- edits the same file, and nothing states when it has grown too large.

- `meshanvil/viewer.py` is 199 lines doing three unrelated jobs: computing the payload, serving it over HTTP, and launching a browser. It is the file the next three endpoints (a data route, an event stream, and the open/reveal route `req_009` needs) would all land in.

- There is no test directory and no test runner. `scripts/selfcheck.py` is 353 lines of hand-rolled asserts covering the whole host codebase in one file, so a single module's behaviour has nowhere of its own to be checked and a failure names the script rather than the unit.
